incident_updates.body: This incident has been resolved, connectivity from AWS to all of our hosts is back to normal.
Connectivity from AWS to Fly.io on impacted hosts is continuing to recover. Approximately 80% of the hosts that were seeing connectivity issues are fully recovered at this time.
AWS has implemented changes to unblock connections from their network from reaching our machines. We are seeing connectivity starting to resume on a host-by-host basis as these changes take effect.

We are continuing to work with our upstream networking partners and AWS on remediation. Impacted customers are recommended to allocate app-scoped static egress IPs using **fly ips allocate-egress.** 

Customers seeing issues are encouraged to also contact AWS support or their AWS hosted vendors support with details of the connection errors and their fly machine IPs.

We are continuing to see connectivity issues from AWS IPs to a subset of our hosts. From our investigation these connections appear to be being blocked from the AWS side. We are continuing to work with our upstream networking partners and AWS on remediation.

In the meantime impacted customers are recommended to allocate app-scoped static egress IPs using **fly ips allocate-egress.**

Our initial investigations indicate connection errors are occuring the return path from AWS IPs. We are escalating the issue with AWS and continuing to investigate. 

Customers seeing issues are encouraged to also contact AWS support or their AWS hosted vendors support with details of the connection errors and their fly machine IPs.
We are investigating reports of elevated networking issues between our network and AWS IPs. We are working to determine the source of the issue.
The congestion affecting our upstream provider has been resolved. We are observing a return to normal levels of networking performance in IAD region.

A subset of hosts in IAD region are experiencing elevated packet loss due to congestion at an upstream provider. We are working with the provider to resolve this issue. Apps hosted in IAD region may experience packet loss at this time.

incidents.name: Elevated errors creating apps and managing secrets

incident_updates.body: Between 06:40 and 09:50 UTC some app creation and secrets requests failed or timed out. Running apps and Machines were not affected.

We’ve applied a fix for the elevated errors affecting app creation and secrets management. Error rates and response times have returned to normal. We’re continuing to monitor to confirm the issue is fully resolved.

We’re seeing elevated error rates and slow responses for some operations that create or change data. Creating new apps, setting or removing secrets, and some app deletions are affected. You may see 500 or 503 errors from `flyctl`, the Machines API, or the dashboard.

Apps and Machines that are already running are not affected. Starting, stopping and reading existing Machines are working normally. We’re investigating and will post another update within 30 minutes.

**Impact**

From about 12:00 to 13:05 UTC, some clients got connection timeouts to their Redis databases. Affected were databases hosted in fra or gig, and clients whose connections were routed through fra or gig, even if their database is hosted in another region.

**What happened**

During a planned rolling upgrade, replicas in fra and gig did not finish draining and were left out of service. They were returned to Fly routing before they were ready to accept connections. Connections routed to them then timed out.

**What we're changing**

• We will be adding tooling to return a replica to service safely after maintenance.

• We will be adding safety checks to our upgrade process.

• We will make the upgrade procedure more resilient to errors like this one.
This incident has been resolved.
A fix has been implemented and we are monitoring the results.
